Concurrent Distributed Worker Pipelines in Go

1. Worker Pool Pattern with Go Channels

In Go, concurrency is coordinated via goroutines and typed channels rather than shared locking structures.

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"sync"
)

type Job struct {
	ID    int
	Input int
}

type Result struct {
	Job   Job
	Value int
}

func worker(id int, jobs <-chan Job, results chan<- Result, wg *sync.WaitGroup) {
	defer wg.Done()
	for j := range jobs {
		// Process computation
		results <- Result{Job: j, Value: j.Input * j.Input}
	}
}

func RunPool(workerCount, jobCount int) {
	jobs := make(chan Job, jobCount)
	results := make(chan Result, jobCount)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup

	for w := 1; w <= workerCount; w++ {
		wg.Add(1)
		go worker(w, jobs, results, &wg)
	}

	for j := 1; j <= jobCount; j++ {
		jobs <- Job{ID: j, Input: j * 10}
	}
	close(jobs)
	wg.Wait()
	close(results)
}
